_comment: Source provenance & license registry. Every field below was checked on 2026-11-23 against the official source unless marked otherwise. license_status values: verified | unclear_needs_review | unknown | not_a_dataset. Do NOT change a status to 'verified' without recording who checked it and the evidence. This file is seeded into the source_registry table by `python -m healthmisinfo.cli seed-registry`.

sources.name: AraFacts (v2, 2024-06-23 update)
sources.license_evidence: LICENSE file at repository root (revision above) contains the full CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code.
sources.redistribution_allowed: non-commercial, with attribution and indication of changes
sources.citation: @inproceedings{arafacts2021, title={AraFacts: The First Large Arabic Dataset of Naturally-Occurring Professionally-Verified Claims}, author={Sheikh Ali, Zien and Mansour, Watheq and Elsayed, Tamer and Al-Ali, Abdulaziz}, booktitle={Proceedings of the Sixth Arabic Natural Language Processing Workshop}, publisher={Association for Computational Linguistics}, year={2021}}
notes: Claims are labelled by professional fact-checkers (Misbar, Fatabyyano, AFP Factuel, Verify-Sy, Maharat-news).

Only 756 of 18,598 claims carry the 'Health' normalized category; this alone cannot reach the 3,000-Arabic target. 5,366 claims are UNCATEGORIZED and may contain further health claims, but adding them requires a human-reviewed health filter.

The authors' normalized 'True' bucket includes 'انتقائي' (selective) and 'مجتزأ' (cut/out-of-context), which are arguably misleading. We therefore map from source_label, not normalized_label, and every mapping entry starts as 'proposed'.
Raw data is NOT committed to this repository; it is fetched by scripts/fetch_datasets.sh into data/raw/ (gitignored).

sources.name: AraCOVID19-MFH V1.0
sources.license_evidence: The official repository contains no LICENSE file and the README states no license; it only asks users to cite the paper. The paper's (Procedia CS, Elsevier) license is NOT the dataset license.
sources.citation: @article{HADJAMEUR2021232, title={AraCOVID19-MFH: Arabic COVID-19 Multi-label Fake News & Hate Speech Detection Dataset}, journal={Procedia Computer Science}, volume={189}, pages={232-241}, year={2021}, doi={10.1016/j.procs.2021.05.086}, author={Mohamed Seghir Hadj Ameur and Hassina Aliane}}
notes: The public release contains ONLY tweet IDs plus 10 label columns; tweet text is not distributed. Text would have to be hydrated through the X (Twitter) API, which requires credentials and is subject to X's developer terms; deleted tweets cannot be recovered.

Labels are multi-label social-media annotations (e.g. Contains_Fake_Information = Yes/No/Maybe/Can't decide). 'No fake information' is NOT the same as 'supported by reliable evidence', so no mapping to the 3-class scheme is assumed. Original labels are preserved as-is.
Requires: (1) written permission or a license from the authors, (2) a lawful hydration route, (3) an approved label mapping, before any training use.

sources.name: PUBHEALTH (Explainable Fact-Checking for Public Health Claims) v1.0
sources.access_method: Official data link in repository data/README.md points to Google Drive file id 1eTtRs5cUlBP5dXsx-FTAlmXuB6JQi2qj (PUBHEALTH.zip with train.tsv/dev.tsv/test.tsv). Google Drive and Hugging Face are NOT reachable from the build environment, so the files must be placed manually in data/manual/pubhealth/.
sources.license_evidence: Repository LICENSE is MIT (Copyright 2020 Neema Kotonya). The data itself is hosted separately on Google Drive; the repository datasheet does not state a separate data license. Claims/explanations originate from third-party fact-checking and news sites (e.g. Snopes, PolitiFact, Reuters), whose own terms may restrict redistribution of their text.
sources.redistribution_allowed: MIT per repository; third-party text redistribution unverified - do not redistribute raw text
sources.citation: @inproceedings{kotonya-toni-2020-explainable, title={Explainable Automated Fact-Checking for Public Health Claims}, author={Kotonya, Neema and Toni, Francesca}, booktitle={Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)}, pages={7740--7754}, year={2020}, publisher={Association for Computational Linguistics}, doi={10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.623}}
notes: Schema above is from the repository documentation; it will be verified by the adapter when the files are provided. The repository README lists test.tsv without a label column, while published loaders include labels for test; the adapter checks the real columns and refuses to guess.
Labels: true / false / mixture / unproven (documented). Mapping to the 3-class scheme starts as 'proposed'.

sources.name: Saudi Ministry of Health open data
sources.access_method: Not reachable from the build environment (network policy). Must be downloaded manually.
sources.license_evidence: Not checked - site not reachable from build environment.
notes: Intended use: contextual EVIDENCE and expert-constructed claims. Any claim constructed from it must be written and reviewed by a qualified human expert, stored with is_synthetic=false only if it is a genuine expert-authored claim, and its provenance recorded. No claims are generated automatically.

sources.name: World Health Organization (fact sheets, Q&A, mythbusters)
sources.access_method: Not reachable from the build environment. Used only as a human-verification reference link.
sources.license_name: WHO copyright; many publications CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (per-document)
sources.license_evidence: Not re-verified in this environment; per-document licensing must be checked.
notes: Shown to users as a place to verify claims. It is never cited as evidence for a specific prediction unless a reviewer attaches a specific URL.

sources.name: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities)
sources.access_method: E-utilities API (eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) - not reachable from the build environment.
sources.license_name: Abstracts subject to publisher copyright; NCBI usage policies apply
notes: Potential evidence-retrieval source for reviewers. Absence of a PubMed hit is never treated as evidence that a claim is false.
